items.title: Sketch to real home
items.prompt: Make a 15s 16:9 real-estate film from my villa clips. Turn one still frame into an architect's pencil sketch (OpenCV line drawing) that draws itself on a sheet of paper lying in 3D, then the paper tilts up and dissolves into the real footage of the same angle. Do it for three angles (facade, double-height hall, living room) with a thin label for each, end on a clean title card. Music only, no whoosh sound effects.

items.title: Map to 3D to real home
items.prompt: 15s 16:9 real-estate reveal: start on a dark map, zoom into the plot, draw the site plan with thin gold lines, extrude it into simple 3D blocks that rise floor by floor, then a light scan wipes the blocks into real footage of the finished villa. Three quiet step labels (Site plan, 3D massing, Built) and a minimal title at the end. Music only.

items.title: Floor-plan tour
items.prompt: 18s 16:9 apartment tour from my room clips, music only. A thin charcoal floor plan draws itself on warm paper, a small camera marker with a view cone enters and walks room to room (living, dining, kitchen, bedroom); each room's footage opens out of the cone and fills the frame while the plan shrinks into a corner inset that highlights the current room. End on 'The Linden Residence · 3 BR · 140 m²'.

items.title: Aerial location pins
items.prompt: 16s 9:16 'location' reel for a residential tower from drone footage, music only. A pin drops on the tower roof with the project name, then thin leader lines and labels pop for nearby places with travel times (International school · 8 min, Metro · 3 min, Beach · 5 min); track each target point with OpenCV so the labels stay locked to the buildings as the drone moves. A gold route line draws along the road to 'Downtown · 12 min'. End on a clean lockup 'MARINA ONE — Coming 2027'.
items.credits: Footage: Đình Luật and other Pexels creators.

items.title: Editorial listing
items.prompt: 17s 9:16 luxury listing in a magazine style from my interior clips, music only. Open on an ivory page where a big serif headline 'Light lives here.' is a window onto the living room, zoom through a letter into full-frame footage, a dining push-in with the spec line '4 Bedrooms — 320 m² — Sea view' appearing word by word, a two-room split, tall columns that open to the bedroom, and end with the villa folding back into a framed window and the lockup 'Maison Aurelle — Private viewing by appointment'. Cut on the beat.

items.title: Perfume, editorial
items.prompt: 16s 9:16 perfume ad from my bottle clips, dark and editorial. Open on a hairline word RAIN, use light-slat wipes and a bento grid of four shots, quick shutter cuts on the beat, end on a lockup 'NOIR / Night Rain'. Very little text, music only.

items.title: Gimbal, HUD callouts
items.prompt: 16s 9:16 tech ad for a phone gimbal. Thin HUD callout lines that follow the product and name one feature each (3-axis stabilised, quick-balance lock, touch screen), a viewfinder frame, smooth push-ins, end with 'Smooth in every frame'. Music only.

items.title: Headphones, text behind
items.prompt: 16s 9:16 headphone ad. Cut the headphones out with rembg and put a giant word QUIET behind them so the product overlaps the letters, a soft line 'Hear every breath of the music', a few polaroid-style frames dropping in, end on 'All sound. No noise.' Music only.

items.title: Sports gear, freeze frame
items.prompt: 16s 9:16 sports ad from tennis clips. STAY FOCUSED on the opening shot, a freeze frame where the player is cut out with a white outline and a giant word behind, an outlined POWER word on impact, a three-panel triptych, a stutter edit on the swing, end on 'Every shot has a purpose'. Music only.

items.prompt: 16s 9:16 drone ad: take-off close-up, then the camera's view widens into aerial shots, thin spec lines appear next to the drone, end with 'SKYLINE MINI / See further.' Clean, little text, music only.

items.title: How big is the Sun?
items.prompt: 17s 9:16 space fact reel, music only. Open on Earth from orbit with the question 'How big is the Sun?'. Over a Milky Way shot, draw Earth and the Sun to true scale, line 109 small Earths across the Sun's width ('109x wider than Earth', '1.3 million Earths would fit inside'), then match the drawn Sun onto a real sunrise above the clouds: 'Its light takes about 8 min to reach us'. Use only facts you are sure of.

items.title: How bees make honey
items.prompt: 19s 9:16 nature explainer from real footage, music only. A honeybee on a flower with a label that follows it, a freeze frame with thin callout lines to the tongue and the honey stomach, then three hive shots with one callout each (passed bee to bee, fanned to dry, capped with wax), end on honey pouring: 'Nectar, made to last.' No numbers, only facts you are sure of.

items.title: How rain is made, cartoon
items.prompt: 19s 9:16 flat cartoon explainer of the water cycle, drawn fully in code, music only. A smiling sun warms the sea, vapor rises (evaporation), cools into a cloud (condensation), the cloud turns grey over the mountains and rains (precipitation), trees perk up and a river carries the water back to the sea (collection). Gentle continuous camera move, short labels, end with the camera pulling back while a loop arrow draws the whole cycle.

items.title: Word-by-word captions
items.prompt: Edit my vertical talking video (video-tho.mp4, 9:16, my English voice is already on it) into a 15–20 second reel with HyperFrames. Keep the strongest lines and cut only on sentence boundaries so the voice stays in sync; the scene changes should feel like clean jump cuts. Get word timings with faster-whisper and add bold, modern word-by-word captions: 2–4 words per line, uppercase heavy sans-serif, white with a dark outline, the word being spoken highlighted on a yellow pill, placed in the lower-middle safe zone and never over my face. Add subtle automatic punch-in zooms (1.0 to about 1.12) on the emphasis words, resetting at each cut. Put a light, calm music bed under the voice so the voice stays clear, and master to about -14 LUFS. Keep it clean: no sound effects, no emoji, counters, progress bars or glow, no AI images, no paid services. Show me a few frames before you render.

items.title: Cut to the beat
items.prompt: Cut these basketball clips into a 16-second vertical (1080x1920) montage that cuts to the beat of a dark trap/electronic track. Run beat detection on the music, and make every cut land on a beat, with the busiest cutting after the drop. Before the big moment, slow the footage right down, then snap back to fast speed on the hit. At the peak, freeze the frame for one beat: darken the background and draw a thin white outline around the player and the ball. Add a short camera shake on the three or four heaviest bass hits only. Use the words "NO DAYS OFF" and nothing else: stack them in a tall condensed font and bring in one word per snare hit during the quiet build. Keep the words off faces and inside the phone safe area. End on a clean dark card that shows the same three words over a faint copy of the player's outline. Play the music only, with no whoosh or pop sound effects. Don't add counters, dots, glow or any other decoration, and keep the footage as the main thing on screen.

items.title: Lighthouse, sunset to night
items.prompt: Make a 16-second vertical (1080x1920) 3D reel drawn entirely in code with Three.js inside HyperFrames, no AI images and no paid services: a flat-shaded low-poly red-and-white lighthouse with a small keeper's cottage, pine trees and a grassy plateau on a faceted rocky island, set in a stylised ocean of animated low-poly waves with foam pieces at the waterline. Play it as a time-lapse from golden sunset to night. The sky gradient moves from gold to coral, magenta, violet and then deep navy, while the sun disc sinks below the horizon, stars fade in one by one and twinkle, and a crescent moon appears. A small sailboat crosses behind the island, bobbing on the waves, and lights a tiny lantern at dusk. Seagulls circle the tower, then drift away as it gets dark. When the lamp turns on, two soft volumetric beams sweep through light fog, and the beams are the only glow. Tower and cottage windows light up one at a time. Use a slow cinematic dolly-in with a slight orbit, rich colour that is sunset-warm and then moonlit-blue, and seeded randomness, with every frame computed from timeline time so the render is deterministic. Add a calm cinematic music bed with fades and no sound effects, put no text on screen, and fade in from black and out to black.

items.title: Tiny room, day to night
items.prompt: Make a 17-second vertical (1080x1920) 3D reel in HyperFrames with Three.js, drawn entirely in code, with no AI images and no paid services. Show an isometric miniature diorama of a cosy tiny room in a pastel, low-poly look, like a premium Blender render. It sits on a cream-and-mint rounded slab over a soft peach background. The room builds itself piece by piece with soft spring bounces: the slab, the wooden floor planks, two walls rising, a window showing a sunset over pink hills, a rug, a bed (frame, mattress, blanket, pillow), a shelf with pastel books and a succulent, a desk with a chair, monitor, keyboard, mug and desk lamp, a framed picture, a big leafy plant by the window, a pouf, a small plant and, last, an orange cat curled up asleep on the bed. Low golden sun comes through the window and leaves a window-shaped patch on the floor, with soft shadows everywhere. Around 9 seconds the sun sinks behind the hills and the sky and background shift from peach through dusk pink to deep indigo, with stars and a crescent moon. The monitor wakes, then the warm desk lamp clicks on with one small flicker and lights the room. The camera orbits slowly and pushes in a little the whole time, the leaves sway and the cat breathes. End with a small italic "Tiny Room" title. Use calm, dreamy lo-fi synth and piano music only, with no sound effects. Keep it deterministic: seeded random, and every frame drawn from timeline time.

items.title: Swiss kinetic type
items.prompt: Make a 16-second 9:16 (1080x1920) kinetic typography reel in HyperFrames (HTML/CSS/GSAP only, no images, no AI art), styled like a Swiss/Bauhaus design-studio poster series. Use the line "Design is how it moves." and give each word its own poster, hard-cut on the beat of a punchy minimal electronic track (about 112 BPM). Use only four flat colours: off-white paper, ink black, signal red and cobalt blue. Use one variable font (Archivo, with weight and width axes) and animate its axes through CSS variables. Give each poster its own shape idea. "Design": the letters arrive sliced into halves over a red circle, go thin and wide, then slam back to heavy and condensed. "is": the i is built from a black bar plus a bouncing red-circle dot, the s rotates in, and a blue half-circle rises. "how": the o is a half-blue disc that drops in and shoves the w aside. "it": the word stretches up from a line, is sliced by a red bar, and the colour field flips from blue to paper. "moves.": stepping ribbons of the word in weights that wave, with one red word fixed in the centre. End on a clean held poster with the full line in heavy condensed type, a red sun, a blue disc, a black rule and two small captions. Use only transform, opacity, clip-path and font-variation animation. Add no numbering, counters, glow or sound effects: music only.

items.title: Pastel domino chain
items.prompt: Make a 17-second vertical (1080x1920) satisfying 3D loop drawn entirely in code with Three.js inside HyperFrames: a soft cream seamless studio sweep, pastel glossy and clay-like shapes (MeshPhysicalMaterial with clearcoat, room-environment lighting, warm key light with soft shadows, neutral tone mapping). A Rube-Goldberg chain cut to the beat of a playful electronic track: a coral ball rolls off a mint tower down a lilac ramp, knocks a rainbow row of ten pastel domino tiles that fall in sequence and lean on each other, the last tile flicks a mint ring that spins like a coin and settles flat, then a blue rounded cube, yellow cylinder, coral cube, small lilac ring and a pink sphere drop one per beat and snap into a neat stack with a little squash, ending on a wide shot of the finished stack with the fallen dominoes trailing behind. All motion precomputed from timeline time (no live physics or randomness), camera cuts on the beat, music only, no sound effects, no text, no glow, counters or decorations.

items.title: Particle morph
items.prompt: Make a 17-second vertical (1080x1920) code-art reel in HyperFrames with Three.js: about 72,000 soft additive point particles (tiny, no glow halos or lens flares, depth of field faked by growing size and lowering alpha away from the focal plane) on a deep dark-blue radial gradient, morphing on the beat of a calm glassy electronic track. Start on a slowly swirling two-arm spiral galaxy with a faint amber core, then sweep (staggered by height, with a little curl turbulence mid-flight) into an open human hand built from a 2D signed-distance silhouette, then into a rotating dotted globe (lat/lon dot grid sampled from hand-drawn continent polygons, a sparse graticule for the ocean, far hemisphere dimmed), then into the word "CODE" sampled from bold type, and finally dissolve the word into flowing divergence-free streams that drift up and fade out. Ice blue and warm white with amber as the only accent, a slow camera dolly with a slight orbit, music only with no sound effects, seeded randomness, and every frame a pure function of timeline time.
